culturalBackground: The back of the hand is the most visible placement for mehndi because it shows whenever the hands are at rest.
Arabic-style trails that run diagonally from the index finger to the wrist are one of the most popular back-hand layouts.
Skin on the back of the hand is thinner than on the palm, so the stain is lighter and fades sooner.
Jewelry-style designs that imitate a hathphool, a ring-and-bracelet hand ornament, are usually drawn on the back of the hand.
applicationTips: Rest the hand flat on a cushion so the skin is taut and the lines stay even.
Start at the fingers and work towards the wrist so your own hand never drags through wet paste.
Leave the paste on longer than you would on the palm, because back-hand skin takes the stain more slowly.

faqPool.q: Why is my back-hand mehndi lighter than my palm?
faqPool.a: The palm has thicker skin, which holds more dye. The back of the hand is thinner, so the stain is lighter and fades faster.

faqPool.q: Which design suits the back of the hand?
faqPool.a: Diagonal trails, a single mandala with decorated fingers, and jewelry-style patterns all work well because they follow the natural lines of the hand.

faqPool.q: How long does back-hand mehndi last?
faqPool.a: Usually about one to two weeks, a little less than the palm, since the back of the hand is washed and exposed more.
